correctness.rationale: Retaining a relaxed Bézout factor c through the Langharst–Wang chord-intersection argument gives the projected bound with factor c^(n-1). Layer-cake integration yields the explicit chord modulus; covariogram polar integration reduces the global estimate to an elementary beta integral and gives the normalized Rogers–Shephard lower bound Psi_n(c). Applying Böröczky’s published stability theorem to the resulting deficit gives the Banach–Mazur estimate. The c=1 case recovers equality throughout, and the relative-inradius extension follows by the same retained-factor Alexandrov–Fenchel argument for inner parallel bodies.

originality.rationale: Langharst–Wang prove the exact constant-one characterization and the special chord and inradius criteria; Böröczky proves quantitative stability for Rogers–Shephard. Searches of mixed-volume Bézout constants, simplex stability, Banach–Mazur distance, longest chords, relative inradii and Rogers–Shephard did not locate the explicit quantitative bridge from the restricted chord-intersection Bézout constant to a Rogers–Shephard deficit or the resulting simplex-distance modulus. Earlier qualitative and isomorphic Bézout results are treated as prior art.

value.rationale: The theorem upgrades a newly completed qualitative characterization to an explicit stability statement using only its minimal special test family. It connects the Bézout defect to a classical affine deficit and then to geometric proximity to a simplex, while also producing explicit directional and relative-inradius moduli and a quantitative obstruction for bodies bounded away from simplices.
